fullPassage: Translating a literary text is challenging, and it's often said there will be an inevitable loss in translation. But that challenge frequently inspires creative re-renderings that offer the prospect of a gain in translation as well. A washing-machine manual doesn't present the same challenges, nor therefore does it inspire the same creativity either. But where, in terms of the opposition between literary and nonliterary language, might we position philosophy's language? Might philosophy want to avoid a translatory economy that aims for a gain in translation but risks a loss? Philosophy wishes to convey its truths intact, without loss—and without gain either, or at least it might hesitate to offer its truths to translation without further clarification of what a gain, and indeed a gain in depth, actually means. It cannot be a matter of offsetting "stylistic losses." The loss philosophy fears is a loss of meaning, the compromising of a truth. Thus, philosophy might refuse to be placed on the side of nonliterary language, and express itself in unstylish language, like Badiou's mathematical writing, so that no translator is prompted to rude and bold acts of creative rewriting. If philosophy wishes to increase its range and avoid being restricted to a national or regional tradition, it needs a translation model that conveys philosophical truths to the world without any "economic" fluctuations of loss and gain.

The loss philosophy fears is a loss of meaning, the ④<u>compromise</u> of a truth.

✅ ② does it inspire: nor 도치 — 정상
✅ ③ hesitate: might + 동사원형 — 정상
det.tip: the compromising of a truth = 진리의 훼손. 동명사의 명사적 용법 (the + -ing + of)

questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칈에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"문학 번역에서 도전은 이득의 __________을 제공하는 창의적 재해석에 영감을 준다."

det.korean: 이득의 전망(prospect)을 제공한다.
det.analysis: ✅ prospect: 'offer the prospect of a gain'에서 직접 확인
det.tip: prospect: 전망, 가능성. offer the prospect of = ~의 가능성을 제공하다

questions.passage: Translating a literary text is challenging. Philosophy wishes to convey its truths intact. Thus, philosophy might refuse to be placed on the side of nonliterary language, and express itself in unstylish language, so that no translator is prompted to rude and bold acts of __________ (create) rewriting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 무례하고 대담한 창의적(creative) 재작성 행위.
det.analysis: ✅ creative: create(동사) → creative(형용사). rewriting을 수식하는 형용사 필요
det.tip: create(v.) → creative(adj.) → creativity(n.) → creatively(adv.)

questions.passage: Translating a literary text is challenging, and it's often said there will be an inevitable loss in translation. But that challenge frequently inspires creative re-renderings that __________. A washing-machine manual doesn't present the same challenges.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[offer / the / prospect / of / a / gain / in / translation / as / well]
questions.wa: offer the prospect of a gain in translation as well
accept: offer the prospect of a gain in translation as well
Offer the prospect of a gain in translation as well
offer the prospect of a gain in translation as well.

det.korean: 번역에서 이득의 전망을 또한 제공하는.
det.analysis: ✅ offer the prospect of a gain in translation as well: offer(제공하다) + the prospect of(~의 전망) + a gain(이득) + in translation(번역에서) + as well(또한)
det.tip: as well = also. 문장 끝에 위치하여 '~도 또한'의 의미

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 빈칸을 채우시오.

"문체적 손실을 상쇄하는 것의 문제가 될 수 없다."
→ It cannot be a matter of __________ "stylistic losses."

det.korean: 문체적 손실을 상쇄하는(offsetting) 것의 문제.
det.analysis: ✅ offsetting: a matter of + -ing(동명사). offset = 상쇄하다, 벌충하다
det.tip: offset: 상쇄하다, 벌충하다. It cannot be a matter of -ing = ~하는 것의 문제가 될 수 없다

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 빈칸을 채우시오.

"철학은 자신의 진리를 온전하게 전달하기를 원한다."
→ Philosophy wishes to __________ its truths intact.

det.korean: 철학은 진리를 온전하게 전달하기를(convey) 원한다.
det.analysis: ✅ convey: wishes to + 동사원형. convey = 전달하다, 운반하다
det.tip: convey: 전달하다, 나르다. convey truths intact = 진리를 온전히 전달하다
